payload.task_text:
Hello, I need to prepare a quarterly portfolio review for our investment committee. The portfolio holds five stocks: AMZN, GOOGL, JNJ, JPM, and XOM. Please look up the stock price data for Q4 2025 (October 1, 2025 through December 31, 2025) for each of these tickers.

For each stock, I need: the closing price on the first trading day of the quarter (start price), the closing price on the last trading day of the quarter (end price), the quarterly return as a percentage rounded to 1 decimal, the highest price during the quarter (quarter high), the lowest price during the quarter (quarter low), and the average daily trading volume.

Create a PowerPoint presentation called Portfolio_Review.pptx in the workspace with the following structure:

A title slide with "Q4 2025 Portfolio Review" as the title and "AMZN, GOOGL, JNJ, JPM, XOM" as the subtitle.

A portfolio overview slide showing which stocks are in the portfolio, the review period, the best performing stock with its return percentage, and the worst performing stock with its return percentage.

One slide for each stock (5 slides total) showing the stock symbol as the title and all the metrics listed above (start price, end price, return, quarter high, quarter low, average volume).

A final "Key Takeaways" slide summarizing the best performer, worst performer, and the average portfolio return across all five stocks rounded to 1 decimal.

Also, please schedule a calendar event for the portfolio review meeting on March 15, 2026 from 2:00 PM to 3:00 PM with title "Q4 2025 Portfolio Review Meeting" and location "Conference Room A".
Note: Use the America/New_York timezone for all calendar events in this task.


Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete it directly in the main agent and dispatch no sub-agent. Five independent Q4 history calls can run natively in parallel, after which one presentation identifier is the only real write dependency.

Resolve the workspace dynamically. In one response call `get_historical_stock_prices` for `AMZN`, `GOOGL`, `JNJ`, `JPM`, and `XOM` natively in parallel with `start_date="2025-10-01"`, `end_date="2026-01-01"`, `interval="1d"`, and `auto_adjust=true` so the end-exclusive API still includes 2025-12-31. For each symbol, sort valid dated rows ascending, reject duplicates/missing closes, use first and last observed trading closes, compute return `(end/start-1)*100`, quarter high/low from the returned adjusted OHLC series, and average daily volume. Freeze one five-row table with source row counts/date bounds and derive best, worst, and simple mean return from unrounded values before display rounding.

In parallel with those reads, call `list_events` for a narrow ISO range covering March 15, 2026 with sufficient `maxResults` and `orderBy="startTime"`, then inspect exact title/time locally. If absent, call `create_event` once with summary `Q4 2025 Portfolio Review Meeting`, start/end local ISO values `2026-03-15T14:00:00`/`2026-03-15T15:00:00`, `timeZone="America/New_York"` in both objects, and location `Conference Room A`; retain its ID for `get_event`. The main agent is the sole presentation writer: create `Portfolio_Review.pptx` once, retain one presentation ID, and build exactly eight slides—title, overview, one per symbol, and Key Takeaways—with all task-requested metrics and one-decimal returns. Do not create a slide per data call or a second deck. Read back slide count, titles, and all five stock metric blocks; read back the event; reconcile best/worst/average values, complete the task, and do not dispatch a verification agent.

nodes.text:
Gather Q4 2025 (October 1, 2025 through December 31, 2025) daily stock price data for these 5 tickers: AMZN, GOOGL, JNJ, JPM, XOM.

Use the Yahoo Finance tool mcp__yahoo-finance__get_historical_stock_prices for each ticker with start_date="2025-10-01", end_date="2025-12-31", interval="1d" (this returns Date, Open, High, Low, Close, Volume per trading day).

For EACH ticker, compute and report:
1. Start price = closing price on the first trading day of the quarter (first trading day on or after 2025-10-01; the date may be 2025-10-01 or later if a holiday/weekend).
2. End price = closing price on the last trading day of the quarter (last trading day on or before 2025-12-31).
3. Quarterly return % = (End price - Start price) / Start price * 100, rounded to 1 decimal place.
4. Quarter high = highest price reached during the quarter (maximum of the High column over the period), rounded to 2 decimals.
5. Quarter low = lowest price reached during the quarter (minimum of the Low column over the period), rounded to 2 decimals.
6. Average daily trading volume = mean of the Volume column across all trading days in the quarter, rounded to the nearest whole number.

Also report the exact date of the first and last trading day for each ticker (they should be identical across all 5 tickers since it's the same market).

Return your findings as a clear structured report with one section per ticker containing all 6 metrics plus the first/last trading day dates. Include the raw numbers precisely (do not round except for the return % to 1 decimal). This data will be used to build a portfolio review presentation, so accuracy matters.
Gather Q4 2025 stock data

Create a PowerPoint presentation file at exactly this path: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-yf-portfolio-ppt-gcal/workspace/Portfolio_Review.pptx

Use the pptx MCP tools (create_presentation, add_slide, populate_placeholder, add_bullet_points, add_table, save_presentation, etc.) to build the presentation, then save it to the path above. The presentation must contain EXACTLY 8 slides in this order:

SLIDE 1 — Title slide:
- Title: "Q4 2025 Portfolio Review"
- Subtitle: "AMZN, GOOGL, JNJ, JPM, XOM"

SLIDE 2 — Portfolio Overview:
- Title: "Portfolio Overview"
- Content should state: the portfolio holds 5 stocks (AMZN, GOOGL, JNJ, JPM, XOM); review period is Q4 2025 (October 1 – December 31, 2025); Best performer: GOOGL with +27.9% return; Worst performer: JPM with +4.2% return. Use bullet points or a small table.

SLIDES 3–7 — One slide per stock, with the stock SYMBOL as the slide title (e.g. "AMZN"), showing these 6 metrics (use a table or labeled bullet list, exact values):
- AMZN: Start price $220.63, End price $230.82, Return +4.6%, Quarter High $258.60, Quarter Low $211.03, Avg Daily Volume 45,111,094
- GOOGL: Start price $244.74, End price $313.00, Return +27.9%, Quarter High $328.62, Quarter Low $235.69, Avg Daily Volume 35,360,358
- JNJ: Start price $183.90, End price $205.86, Return +11.9%, Quarter High $214.05, Quarter Low $180.82, Avg Daily Volume 8,526,356
- JPM: Start price $307.82, End price $320.77, Return +4.2%, Quarter High $329.37, Quarter Low $289.24, Avg Daily Volume 8,613,502
- XOM: Start price $110.28, End price $119.54, Return +8.4%, Quarter High $120.99, Quarter Low $108.71, Avg Daily Volume 14,262,136

SLIDE 8 — Key Takeaways:
- Title: "Key Takeaways"
- Content: Best performer: GOOGL (+27.9%); Worst performer: JPM (+4.2%); Average portfolio return across all five stocks: +11.4% (rounded to 1 decimal).

Notes on formatting: Use a clean professional look (e.g., a default business template/color scheme). Prices should be formatted with a dollar sign and 2 decimals, returns with a +/− sign and 1 decimal, volumes with thousands separators. Make sure every required value appears on its slide. After saving, verify the file exists at the target path and confirm the final file path in your report.
